newsitem.title: TURKEY: Six injured in Turk ammunition factory explosions.
newsitem.headline: Six injured in Turk ammunition factory explosions.

text.p: At least six people were injured on Thursday in a series of explosions at a state-owned ammunition factory in central Turkey, local officials said.

Anatolian news agency said the first blast occured at 8.50 a.m. (0550 GMT) and was followed by a series of intermittent explosions. A fire in the factory continues to rage and a thick cloud of smoke billowed above the area, witnesses said.

They said the southern district of Kirikkale town had been evacuated and the windows of buildings had been shattered. Nearby streets were crowded with traffic as people left the area for other parts of the town, they said.
An official at the governor's office told Reuters a call had been made for people to leave the area.
Turkey's interior, defence and industry ministers arrived in the town and entered a crisis committee meeting with the regional governor to consider how to deal with the situation, Anatolian said.
Six factory workers were injured, one of them seriously in the blast, Anatolian said. It did not say why the explosions took place.
A fireman speaking by phone from Kirikkale fire station said the nature of the factory made it impossible to approach it on the ground.
"There are enough explosives in this factory to blow up the whole town. It is not possible to approach the factory," he told Reuters.
Fire-fighting helicopters were being sent to the area, Anatolian said.
State oil refiner Tupras has a refinery in the area, but it was far enough away not to be affected by the explosions, a top Tupras official told Reuters.
But he said filling activities had been halted temporarily as a precaution.
